license_required.quote: Practice optometry in this state without having a valid, unrevoked, and unexpired license certificate and annual renewal registration certificate as an optometrist.

age_minimum.quote: Every person desiring to practice optometry in this state shall be 19 years of age, or over

degree_required.value: Doctor of Optometry degree from accredited school or college of optometry requiring at least four years of professional study, with minimum three years of preoptometry at accredited college or university
degree_required.quote: have a minimum of three years of preoptometry, or the equivalent, at an accredited college or university, have completed a course of study in an accredited school or college of optometry which is approved by the board and that requires at least four years of professional study

exams.name: Standard examination
exams.quote: have passed all examinations prescribed by the board, which may include the standard examination after completion of the educational requirements. The board may accept a passing grade on a recognized national examination or a passing grade on a board examination, or both, and may require a passing grade on additional state law examinations.

exams.name: National Board of Examiners in Optometry
exams.quote: all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry

interval_years.quote: annually, on or before the first day of October, pay to the secretary of the board a renewal fee

renewal_fee_usd.quote: pay to the secretary of the board a renewal fee of one hundred sixty dollars ($160)

required.quote: All registered optometrists licensed in this state are required to take annual courses of study in subjects relating to the practice of optometry.

hours_per_period.quote: The length of study shall be prescribed by the board but shall not exceed 25 hours in any calendar year.

value: For optometrists approved to use pharmaceutical agents: 20-25 hours total, with at least half in diagnosis, treatment, and management of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures
topical_requirements.quote: Licensees approved by the board to use pharmaceutical agents shall be required to take not less than 20 nor more than 25 hours of continuing education, half of which shall be in subjects relating to the diagnosis, treatment, and management of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures.

available.quote: Any person who has successfully passed a standard examination in optometry in any state of the United States or all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry and is the holder of a certificate to that effect, issued by the board of that state, or by the national board, and who has a current license to practice optometry in any state in the United States, and has conducted an ethical professional practice of optometry for at least one year, may, at the discretion of the board, and upon the payment of the amount of the regular examination fee, take the standard examination, and upon passing the examination be registered as qualified to practice optometry in this state.

requirements.value: Must have passed standard examination in another state or all parts of NBEO examination; must hold current license in another state; must have conducted ethical professional practice for at least one year; must pass Alabama standard examination upon payment of regular examination fee
requirements.quote: Any person who has successfully passed a standard examination in optometry in any state of the United States or all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry and is the holder of a certificate to that effect, issued by the board of that state, or by the national board, and who has a current license to practice optometry in any state in the United States, and has conducted an ethical professional practice of optometry for at least one year, may, at the discretion of the board, and upon the payment of the amount of the regular examination fee, take the standard examination

national_certification.value: National Board of Examiners in Optometry (NBEO)
national_certification.quote: all parts of the examination given by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry

regulatory_model.quote: Practice optometry in this state without having a valid, unrevoked, and unexpired license certificate and annual renewal registration certificate as an optometrist.

credential_type.quote: the board shall grant to qualified applicants a license and a license certificate

is_mandatory.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to perform any of the following: (1) Practice optometry in this state without having a valid, unrevoked, and unexpired license certificate and annual renewal registration certificate as an optometrist.

title_protection.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to perform any of the following: (1) Practice optometry in this state without having a valid, unrevoked, and unexpired license certificate

scope_protection.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to perform any of the following: (1) Practice optometry in this state without having a valid, unrevoked, and unexpired license certificate and annual renewal registration certificate as an optometrist.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or misrepresentation in practice or obtaining license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or misrepresentation, whether knowingly or unknowingly, in the practice of optometry or in obtaining any license, license certificate, annual registration certificate, or other thing of value.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of a felony or a misdemeanor which involves moral turpitude.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual drunkenness or addiction to morphine, cocaine, or similar drugs
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual drunkenness or addiction to the use of morphine, cocaine, or other drugs having similar effect.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Insanity as adjudged by court of competent jurisdiction
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Insanity, as adjudged by a court of competent jurisdiction.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Directly or indirectly employing, hiring, procuring, or inducing unlicensed person to practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Directly or indirectly employing, hiring, procuring, or inducing a person, not licensed to practice optometry in this state, to so practice.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Directly or indirectly aiding or abetting unlicensed practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Directly or indirectly aiding or abetting in the practice of optometry any person not duly licensed to practice under this chapter.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Directly or indirectly employing solicitors, canvassers, or agents for obtaining patronage
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Directly or indirectly employing solicitors, canvassers, or agents for the purpose of obtaining patronage.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully or repeatedly violating chapter provisions
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully or repeatedly violating any of the provisions of this chapter.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing or attempting to practice under name other than own name on license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing or attempting to practice optometry under a name other than one's own name as set forth on the license certificate.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Lending, leasing, renting, or placing license at disposal of unlicensed person
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Lending, leasing, renting, or in any other manner placing his or her license or license certificate at the disposal or in the service of any person not licensed to practice optometry in this state.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Soliciting patients by fraudulent or misleading advertising
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Soliciting patients by fraudulent or misleading advertising of any kind, nature, or description.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to comply with continuing education requirements
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to comply with the continuing education requirements established by the board pursuant to the provisions of this chapter.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing in temporary office apart from regularly established office (with exceptions for branch offices)
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing optometry in any temporary office, apart from a regularly established office; provided, that a licensed optometrist may establish a branch office if the branch office is duly equipped with the instruments necessary, according to rules and regulations promulgated by the board, to make complete optometric examination

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing as employee on basis of fee splitting or similar arrangement (with exceptions for HMOs and partnerships)
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing optometry as the employee of any person, group, association, or corporation on the basis of any fee splitting or on any basis which has the effect of any such agreement; provided, that the provisions of this subdivision shall not be so construed as to prohibit a licensed optometrist from participating in health maintenance organizations composed of licensed professional practitioners in the health care field, other similar ethical professional health care groups, or in professional associations or professional corporations organized under Alabama law

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating other standards of professional conduct adopted as rules by board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating any other standards of professional conduct as may be adopted as rules by the board.

definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry is a learned profession involving the examination, measurement by objective and subjective means, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of any departure from the normal of the human eyes, their adjacent structures, and visual system. The practice of optometry includes but is not limited to: The adapting and fitting of all types of lenses or devices, including, contact lenses; the determination of refractive error and shape of the eye and visual, muscular, or anatomical anomalies of the eye through the use of any means including the use of any self testing devices and the use of any computerized or automatic refracting device; the determination and prescribing of spectacle or contact lens parameters; the administering and prescription of pharmaceutical agents rational to the diagnosis and treatment of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures; the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and its adjacent structures; the providing of developmental and perceptual therapy for the vision system; the utilization of any method or means to diagnose and treat diseases of the human eye and its adjacent structures as determined and approved by the board, subject to the limitations of this chapter; the performance of primary eye care procedures or ordering of laboratory tests rational to the diagnosis and treatment of conditions or disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures as determined and approved by the board, subject to the limitations of this chapter.

drug_authority.value: Optometrists may prescribe and administer pharmaceutical agents for diagnosis and treatment of disease of the human eye and adjacent structures, including narcotic analgesics (except Schedule I and II), Schedule III agents (limited to 96 hours except hydrocodone), steroids, and medications to counteract anaphylaxis. Use of pharmaceutical agents limited to board-approved optometrists.
drug_authority.quote: The administering and prescription of pharmaceutical agents rational to the diagnosis and treatment of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures; ... The practice of optometry shall include the prescribing and administering of narcotic analgesics pursuant to the Alabama Uniform Controlled Substances Act, except for narcotic analgesics classified under Schedule I and II, and any Schedule III pharmaceutical agents that contain Dihydrocodeinone, ('Hydrocodone'). The prescribing or administering of any other Schedule III pharmaceutical agent shall be limited to a prescription, the duration of which does not exceed 96 hours. Notwithstanding any provision of this chapter to the contrary, the practice of optometry shall include the prescribing and administering of pharmaceutical agents which are commonly known as steroids. ... The practice of optometry shall include the authority to administer benedryl, epinephrine, or other medication to counteract anaphylaxis or anaphylactic reaction. The use and prescribing of pharmaceutical agents for the treatment of the human eye and its adjacent structures shall be limited to those optometrists approved by the board.

surgery_prohibited.quote: Optometrists are prohibited from performing injections into the eyeball, cataract surgery, muscle surgery, retinal surgery, radial keratotomy, laser surgery, cryosurgery, or any other invasive surgery.

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and its adjacent structures

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: The practice of optometry shall include the authority to administer benedryl, epinephrine, or other medication to counteract anaphylaxis or anaphylactic reaction.

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: the providing of developmental and perceptual therapy for the vision system

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: The use and prescribing of pharmaceutical agents for the treatment of the human eye and its adjacent structures shall be limited to those optometrists approved by the board.

pharmacology_training_hours_required.quote: the requirement that the applicant has successfully completed at least 72 clock hours in the diagnosis and management of disease of the human eye and its adjacent structures within a three-year period preceding application for a license.

delegation_to_unlicensed_assistants_auth.quote: A provider may delegate tasks and activities at an established treatment site to an assistant who is properly trained and supervised or directed.

telemedicine_authorized.quote: A health service that is delivered by a licensed optometrist acting within the scope of his or her license and that requires the use of advanced telecommunications technology, other than telephone or facsimile technology

home_visit_permit_required.quote: A patient's private home is not considered an established treatment site.

impaired_practitioner_program_establishe.quote: The Alabama Board of Optometry approved or sponsored program for the detection, intervention, and monitoring of impaired providers.

limited_teaching_license_available.quote: The board, by rule, may issue a limited teaching license to teachers who hold an optometric degree and are not licensed and registered to practice optometry in this state.

retired_license_status_available.quote: The board may waive annual registration and the payment of fees while any licensee is prevented from practicing optometry by reason of physical disability, temporary active duty with any of the Armed Forces of the United States, or while any licensee is completely retired from the practice of optometry.

jurisprudence_exam_required.quote: may require a passing grade on additional state law examinations
